Audio panel transmit keys (S_ASP*_SEND) are a radio group: pressing CAB SEND on ASP2 deselected VHF 1 SEND. One var cannot restore the group; the pilot pressed VHF 1 SEND again. For sync: the SEND keys of a panel must be treated as one group (and the lamp I_ASP*_SEND of every key watched).

S_OH_ELEC_BUSTIE OFF disconnects EXT PWR and Fenix does not reconnect it when BUS TIE returns to AUTO; the pilot must press EXT PWR again. For sync this means a BUS TIE write on one side can drop ground power there, and a restore is not enough.

S_MIP_CLOCK_CHR: CHR starts and stops the chrono, RST resets it (pilot correction). The key is a press counter (it read 8 after the pilot's clicks). One key cannot restore the clock, so clock keys are skipped.

S_COCKPIT_DOOR (positions 0,1,2 found): after stepping and restoring the switch, I_OH_DOOR_CTL_U and I_PED_COCKPIT_DOOR_U went from lit to off, but the pilot confirms the door never closed. Those lamps show lock/fault state, not door open. Restore check could not pass; the pilot accepted the state. Both cockpit door switches skipped afterwards.

The pilot's Fenix option that links the captain and FO EFIS (single-pilot use) was on for the first part of the buttons phase: S_FCU_EFIS1_BARO_MODE/BARO_STD and FD acted on both sides. The option was switched off; the BARO keys were re-tested. For Crosscheck this per-pilot option changes what a key does and must be checked at session start.

S_FCU_EFIS1_FD: one probe press switched both FDs off (EFIS sync was on); the restore press did not bring them back, and afterwards a pilot click shows FD on only while pressed (the FD keys read 2 after one click: press counters). Fenix's FD state looks out of step after the probe's 1/0 writes. FDs left off for the rest of the run, to be fixed by the pilot afterwards. FD keys skipped.

S_EXT_GPU_PLUG is a click var: writing 1 pulled the GPU plug and the aircraft lost ground power; it reads 0 both plugged and unplugged. Must never be synced as a state. S_OH_ELEC_EXT_PWR is a press counter too (a pilot press moved it 2 -> 4).

BLOWER and EXTRACT FAULT lights (I_OH_PNEUMATIC_BLOWER_U, I_OH_PNEUMATIC_EXTRACT_U) came on when ground power dropped (BUS TIE test) and went out by themselves about 10 minutes later, during the cargo FWD ISOL VALVE test. Recorded as a delayed recovery, not a valve effect.

Probe bug found and fixed: in the buttons phase S_FCU_EFIS2_ND_MODE (rest value 3) took the press-counter path, was written 4 and 5 and wrongly counted as restored (same parity). It stayed at 5 until the supervised ND check noticed; then written back to 3 with the undo command. The buttons test now writes nothing to a var resting above 1 unless it is MASTER CAUTION/WARNING.

Fenix WASM crash during the probe. Last real reaction: S_PED_RMP3_XFER at 14:16:39 UTC. The next test stepped S_COCKPIT_DOOR through 0..7 (3..7 are not positions); its lamps went dark and did not come back, while the pilot saw the door unchanged. Every later write was stored but nothing reacted and GraphQL returned nothing for switches. Most likely cause: writing a non-existent position to S_COCKPIT_DOOR (the earlier write of 5 to S_FCU_EFIS2_ND_MODE at 14:13:35 was followed by normal reactions, so it is less likely). All results after 14:16:40 UTC are marked invalid: the remaining positions, all encoders, all breakers and the takeover checks. Strong support for the rule: never write a value outside the profile's allowed set, also in test tools.

S_OH_HYD_YELLOW_ELEC_PUMP is a press counter (a hand click moves it 0 -> 2), not a 0/1 switch. Absolute writes do not undo a press. Any Fenix pushbutton may be like this; the probe now restores with one more press when writing the old value back does not undo the effect, and marks such vars counter-suspected.
